implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (approved 2026-09-17, effective 2026-10-01) now covers OT explicitly; the 2024 policy was written for IT. OT access procedures for the plant HMIs and jump hosts are being rewritten under STD-04.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a general: review cyber security procedures annually); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 R1 Part 1.2.3)

implementation_statement: ROC SCADA uses named operator, engineer, and viewer accounts in the SCADA domain, created on a ticket approved by the ROC Manager. Gaps: the Pine Hollow and Sawgrass Run plant HMIs use shared operator accounts (gap 6), and OT account reviews are annual. P07 found 3 of 25 sampled leavers still enabled in the SCADA domain 9 to 40 days after departure.
evidence: SCADA domain export 2026-08-04; HMI user lists; P07 AC-2 sample
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation); C-DAMS-R01 (Table 9.3b access control)

implementation_statement: Corporate accounts are provisioned and disabled automatically from the HR feed. The SCADA domain is separate and manual; the HR termination notice reaches the OT Security Manager by email.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: Planned: disable SCADA domain and jump host accounts after 35 days of inactivity, with a monthly report to the ROC Manager (STD-04, due 2027-03-31). Today no inactivity rule exists in OT.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: Account creation, change, and disablement in the SCADA domain and on the jump hosts are logged to the SIEM for the ROC and Blackwater Bend. Plant HMI account changes at Cedar Shoals, Pine Hollow, and Sawgrass Run are not logged centrally.
evidence: SIEM use case list; SCADA domain audit policy
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a intrusion detection and response)

implementation_statement: SCADA roles enforce what each account can do: operators command gates and units, engineers change logic and displays, viewers only watch. RMOS client screens are limited by client. Gap: plant HMIs at PNH and SGR give every shared-account user full operator rights.
evidence: SCADA role matrix; HMI configuration review
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: Site OT firewalls and the OT DMZ control flows to and from the corporate network: the historian replica pushes one way to the cloud data lake, and corporate users reach OT only through the jump hosts. Gaps: the OT WAN is routed flat between sites, and RMOS client tunnels terminate in the same ROC SCADA zone that controls company gates (gap 2).
evidence: OT firewall rule exports (5 sites); network diagram rev. 2026-07
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 3.1)

implementation_statement: Operator and engineer roles are separate in SCADA, and logic changes need a second engineer. The OT Security Manager reports to the system owner, so OT security checks its own work; compensated by the co-sourced internal audit firm and the NERC Compliance Manager reporting to the General Counsel.

Engineering rights are limited to 24 controls engineering and I&C staff. Privileged access management covers only the cloud accounts; local administrator accounts on OT Windows hosts are shared within controls engineering and rotated twice a year.
evidence: Local admin inventory; PAM scope document

implementation_statement: Engineers use separate administrator accounts on the jump hosts and SCADA servers. At the plants, engineers use the same account for email-free engineering work and administration.
SCADA domain administrator rights are held by 4 named engineers. Local administrator passwords on 29 OT Windows hosts at PNH and SGR are shared.
Privileged actions on ROC SCADA servers and jump hosts are logged to the SIEM. Not at the plants outside BWB.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a intrusion detection and response)

control_name: Prohibit Non-privileged Users from Executing Privileged Functions
implementation_statement: SCADA and HMI software prevents operator and viewer roles from changing logic, setpoint limits, or alarm settings.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: SCADA and jump hosts lock an account for 15 minutes after 5 failed sign-ins. PLCs and gate panels cannot enforce this and are protected by physical access and network segmentation instead.
Jump hosts and ROC consoles show a use notice before sign-in. Plant HMIs at PNH and SGR do not.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: Engineering workstations and jump hosts lock after 15 minutes. Operator consoles in staffed control rooms are exempt by design, so alarms stay visible; the control rooms are card-access areas.
evidence: Group policy export; tailoring note in this SSP
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: Jump host sessions end after 30 minutes of inactivity and after 8 hours in total.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: Staff and most vendors reach OT only through the jump hosts in the OT DMZ with MFA (since 2025). evidence: Jump host configuration; OT firewall VPN profiles; P07 walkthrough
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation; Form 3 Q12); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 6)

regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a; Form 3 Q12c (vendor activity logs reviewed at least weekly))

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions use TLS to the jump hosts; RMOS client and OEM tunnels use IPsec with certificates.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: Jump hosts are the managed access point for staff. The 2 OEM VPNs and the Sawgrass Run modem are unmanaged access points.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 3.1)

implementation_statement: Remote privileged commands to SCADA are allowed only from jump host sessions approved by the ROC shift supervisor; the OEM VPNs allow direct engineering access.

Microwave links are encrypted. River gauge modems use the private APN, but 3 of 9 still had default web passwords at P07 testing.
Mobile devices and field services laptops may not connect to OT networks; OT switch ports are disabled when unused at the ROC and BWB.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: RMOS client sites are external systems connected by site-to-site VPN. Client contracts do not define security responsibilities or incident notice (gap 9). Field crews connect company laptops to client equipment only under client supervision.
evidence: Client contract template; field services procedure

implementation_statement: Corporate annual awareness training for all users, plus quarterly CIP-003 cyber security reinforcement for staff with access to BWB, CDS, and the ROC. Completion 96% in 2025.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a training); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 1)

implementation_statement: Insider threat awareness module for OT and security staff planned for 2027 Q1 (Form 3 Q32b).

ROC operators receive annual role-based OT security training. Plant operators at PNH and SGR and the I&C technicians have not (gap in Table 9.3a training for "individuals with significant control systems security roles").
Training completion is recorded in the LMS and kept for 3 years to support CIP-003 evidence.

Logged events: SCADA sign-ins, commands, and configuration changes; jump host sessions; OT firewall allows and denies at all 5 sites. Plant HMIs and engineering laptops at CDS, PNH, and SGR are not logged centrally.
evidence: SIEM source list; firewall log settings
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a intrusion detection; Form 3 Q14a)

implementation_statement: The SCADA event journal records time, user, console, object, old and new value for every command and setpoint change.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews SIEM alerts 24x7; OT security engineers review jump host vendor sessions weekly. OEM VPN activity and plant HMI logs outside BWB are not reviewed.
evidence: MSSP monthly reports; weekly review log

implementation_statement: SIEM correlation covers identity, cloud, corporate, and OT sensor alerts from the ROC and BWB.
IT and OT alerts land in one SIEM, so a phishing compromise and a jump host sign-in can be correlated. OT coverage stops at BWB.
GPS time sources at the ROC and each plant feed SCADA, PLCs, and firewalls; the SIEM normalizes to UTC.
Logs forwarded to the SaaS SIEM cannot be changed by OT administrators. The SCADA journal is protected by SCADA domain permissions.
SIEM keeps 1 year searchable; the SCADA journal keeps 90 days on the server and 3 years in the historian archive. Plant HMI logs at PNH and SGR roll over after about 14 days.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Form 3 Q14a); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-012-2 and CIP-003-9 evidence retention of 3 calendar years)

implementation_statement: Audit generation is enabled on ROC and BWB systems and on every OT firewall; not on the 29 Windows hosts at PNH and SGR.
The co-sourced internal audit firm assesses OT and IT controls each year (P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-28); an outside OT firm performs annual vulnerability assessments at the ROC and BWB.
evidence: P07 plan and results; 2025-10 OT assessment report

implementation_statement: Assessors report to the audit committee and do not design or operate the assessed controls.
The ICCP link has a written interconnection agreement with the BA/TOP. RMOS client tunnels have no interconnection terms (gap 9); the two OEM VPNs have none.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a general (review network connections, not to exceed 18 months)); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-012-2 R1 Part 1.5)

implementation_statement: P07 POA&M tracks every weakness with an owner and date; the Section 9 subset is the plan and schedule sent to the Regional Engineer on 2026-09-30.
evidence: poam.csv; letter to the Regional Engineer
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A 9.1.1.3 (plan and schedule for negative Form 3 responses))

implementation_statement: The COO, as authorizing official equivalent, accepted operation of the HCDMS with conditions on 2026-09-17 (section 4.2).
Monthly OT security metrics go to the system owner; the MSSP reports monthly. Coverage is limited to the ROC and BWB.
No OT penetration test has been done. A test against the SCADA vendor test system at the ROC and the OT DMZ is planned for 2027 Q2.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3b vulnerability assessment (non-production where appropriate))

implementation_statement: Connections between ROC SCADA and plant controllers are not restricted by site; any plant host can reach controllers at other plants (gap 2).
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: Baseline configurations exist for ROC SCADA servers, consoles, and BWB plant systems. CDS, PNH, and SGR baselines are incomplete (gap 7).

control_name: Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency
implementation_statement: Automated configuration comparison for PLCs and HMIs planned with the OT monitoring expansion (2027 Q2).
PLC and HMI configurations are backed up monthly to the OT backup server and quarterly to offline media, complete only for the ROC and BWB.
OT changes go through the controls engineering change board with ROC Manager approval. Security review is not a required step, and OEM changes made over the direct VPNs bypass the board.

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: SCADA changes are tested on the vendor-supplied test system at the ROC before release.
Engineering impact analysis is done for every change; security impact analysis is not (POL-01 4.9 now requires it).
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a system lifecycle (secure design and modification))

implementation_statement: Only controls engineering can load PLC logic at the ROC and BWB; at PNH and SGR the shared HMI accounts and the OEM VPNs allow changes.
Hardened settings applied to ROC servers and jump hosts from the SCADA vendor guide. Plant hosts at PNH and SGR run default settings on unsupported operating systems.
Unneeded services removed on ROC servers. Engineering laptops at the plants carry general tools.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control (approved control system activities only))

implementation_statement: Application allowlisting on ROC SCADA servers and consoles; not at the plants.
The OT asset inventory is complete for the ROC and BWB (612 assets). CDS, PNH, and SGR are partial (gap 1). P07 found an undocumented cellular modem at SGR.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A 9.2 (accurate inventory of cyber assets); Form 3 Q9a-9b, Q19a)

implementation_statement: New assets are added through the change board; field changes by OEMs are not always reported.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a general (criticality determined as new assets are added))

implementation_statement: Passive OT sensors at the ROC and BWB alert on new devices; none at CDS, PNH, or SGR (gap 4).
Users cannot install software on OT hosts; installs go through controls engineering.

The OT contingency procedures cover hardware failure and failover to the backup ROC. They do not cover recovery after a cyber attack, and the BWB Rapid Recovery sub-element does not cover ROC SCADA recovery (gap 7).
evidence: OT contingency procedure rev. 2024; BWB Security Plan

implementation_statement: Contingency procedures reference the EAPs, but cyber triggers for EAP actions are missing (gap 8).

Local control resumes the essential missions (gate operation, warning) within minutes; restoration of central control after a cyber event has no defined sequence outside the P08 runbook drafted in 2026.
Operators are trained and drilled on local gate and unit operation each year with the EAP readiness test. Cyber contingency training does not exist yet.
A restore test passed at BWB in 2025 (unit PLC and HMI rebuilt on spare hardware in 6 hours). No tests at CDS, PNH, SGR, or for the ROC SCADA.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a restoration and recovery (annual testing of plan))

implementation_statement: The annual EAP readiness tests do not include a cyber scenario.
Quarterly offline media copies of PLC and HMI configurations are kept in the ROC records vault, 40 miles from Cedar Shoals. Incomplete for 3 plants.

The backup ROC in the Cedar Shoals powerhouse can take over supervision in about 90 minutes. It shares the SCADA domain and flat OT WAN with the primary, so it does not protect against a cyber event (P05 finding 2).

Fiber with licensed microwave backup to every project; satellite phones at the ROC and BWB. The ICCP link to the BA/TOP runs on one leased circuit, and the CIP-012 plan lacks loss and recovery methods (gap 11).
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A 7.2 (communication redundancies)); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-012-2 R1 Parts 1.2 and 1.3)

implementation_statement: SCADA servers are imaged weekly to the OT backup server; PLC and HMI configurations monthly; historian data replicates to the cloud. Governor settings for 5 units (PNH 3, SGR 2) are held only by the OEMs.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a restoration and recovery; Form 3 Q16)

implementation_statement: Backups are verified by checksum. Restore testing only at BWB.
Recovery to a known-good state is documented for BWB only. The 2-hour RTO for gate supervisory control (P05) is unproven elsewhere.
Unique SCADA domain accounts at the ROC and BWB. Shared operator accounts on the PNH and SGR plant HMIs (gap 6).
MFA for all privileged remote access through the jump hosts. No MFA on the 2 OEM VPNs or on local engineering consoles.
MFA for all corporate users and all jump host users. Local console sign-in in control rooms is password only (card-access rooms).
Push MFA with number matching resists replay.
RMOS client gateways and OEM tunnels authenticate with certificates. Devices on plant OT LANs are not authenticated (no port security outside the ROC and BWB).
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: SCADA identifiers are unique and never reused; RMOS client users are guests in the identity provider.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control and functional segregation)

implementation_statement: SCADA passwords need 14 characters and change yearly. P07 found default passwords on the SGR modem and on 3 river gauge modems.
SCADA domain and jump hosts check passwords against a banned list.
RMOS client users sign in to the portal as guests through the company identity provider with MFA.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a access control (guests and customers))

implementation_statement: IT incident training for the IT team and the MSSP; OT incident roles not yet trained outside the ROC.
Tabletop on 2024-09-18 met the CIP-003 36-month test. It did not involve gate operations, the EAP, law enforcement, or RMOS clients.
IT incidents are handled by the IT Director with the MSSP. OT incident handling is in draft P08 runbooks (2026-09).
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a intrusion detection and response); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 4.4)

implementation_statement: Incidents are tracked in the MSSP ticketing system and the company incident log.
The CIP-003 plan defines Reportable Cyber Security Incident determination and E-ISAC notice. The plan does not tie a cyber event on gates or units to 18 CFR 12.10 reporting (gap 8).
MSSP incident response retainer; breach counsel and forensics through the cyber insurer panel.
Cyber security incident response plan (2024) covers the low impact BES assets. It lacks EAP linkage and crisis management for a ransomware event that forces IT/OT separation (gap 8).
Maintenance on control equipment is scheduled and recorded in the EAM.
Company-managed transient laptops have EDR and are scanned before use at BES assets (CIP-003 Section 5.1). Vendor laptops at PNH and SGR are not checked.

Nonlocal maintenance goes through the jump hosts with MFA and recording, except the 2 OEM VPNs. At CDS there is no method to detect malicious communications in vendor sessions (CIP-003-9 Section 6.3).
On-site vendor technicians are escorted in control rooms and powerhouses.
Removable media is restricted to controls engineering; offline backup media is kept in the ROC vault.
Media and decommissioned OT equipment are wiped or destroyed with certificates.
Media scanning kiosks at the ROC, BWB, and CDS (CIP-003 Section 5.3). PNH and SGR have none.
Card access lists for control rooms, spillway gate houses, and powerhouses are approved by plant managers and reviewed quarterly.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a general (physical security)); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 2)

implementation_statement: Fencing, locked gate houses, card access, and intrusion detection at all 4 projects and the ROC, monitored by the security operations desk. Gate PLC panels are inside locked gate houses.
regulatory_driver: C-DAMS-R01 (Rev. 3A Table 9.3a general; Form 1 Q6); C-DAMS-R03 (CIP-003-9 Att. 1 Sec. 2)

implementation_statement: Cameras and alarms are monitored 24x7; video analytics (AI-003) at BWB and CDS.
Visitor logs kept for control rooms and powerhouses for 1 year.
Standby generators power gate hoists; tested annually under 18 CFR 12.54.
evidence: Gate and standby power test records 2026

ROC servers patched quarterly after vendor qualification. No patch cadence at the plants (gap 5).
EDR on ROC Windows servers and consoles; legacy antivirus with stale signatures on PNH and SGR hosts.
Passive OT network monitoring at the ROC and BWB with MSSP alerting. No monitoring at CDS, PNH, or SGR (gap 4).

E-ISAC member; CISA ICS advisories reviewed weekly; HSIN Dams portal account held by the Corporate Security Manager.

OT supply chain risk management plan due 2027-03-31 (STD-03).
